title: Industry Leading Implementation Plan

axiomatic: Rooms must be physically grounded architectural volumes rather than flat symbolic placeholders
Openings, cutaways, and interior visibility must derive from the room's actual physical structure
Future procedural object placement must depend on stable room-local geometry and metadata
axiological: Prioritize realism, spatial credibility, maintainability, and high-performance rendering
Preserve visual fidelity while preventing temporal instability or unnecessary complexity
Prefer systems that remain extensible for future procedural content
teleological: Evolve the scene toward an architecture system with thick shells, procedural openings, and room-local placement anchors
Enable future windows, doors, cutaways, and procedural interior objects without redesigning the foundation
Deliver a visually convincing and ultra-stable room system that can scale across room types

objectives: Make node surfaces look more physically plausible
Prepare for a future shader-based rain pass
Rebuild rooms as thick-shell physical volumes with procedural openings
Enable future procedural interior object placement with stable anchors and clearance zones
Support windows, doors, and cutaways as true structural features
qualityGuards: Preserve visual fidelity while preventing temporal instability such as shimmer, flicker, crawling noise, and specular popping
Keep rendering changes GPU-friendly and avoid unnecessary CPU-side work in hot paths
Prefer graceful degradation of secondary effects over visible instability in primary shading
Apply LOD-aware shading and effect simplification for distant or low-salience surfaces without reducing close-up quality
Validate visual changes against regression cases to avoid over-tuning, banding, or unnatural surface response
Keep room geometry deterministic, reproducible, and derived from a single authoritative room definition
Separate physical shell data, visual cutaway state, and future placement metadata so they do not drift apart
Avoid brittle ad hoc cutout logic by using parametric openings and stable local coordinate rules

workstreams.name: PBR shader tuning
goals: Add analytic SDF normals and subtle surface variation
Make wetness affect roughness, albedo, and reflectance

phases.name: Physically based material structure
tasks: Define baseColor, metalness, roughness, specularF0, clearcoat, clearcoatRoughness, normalStrength, ambientOcclusion, and emissive fields
Create a consistent material contract for SDF-rendered surfaces
Keep all parameters artist-friendly and scene-consistent

phases.name: Lighting model upgrade
tasks: Implement GGX specular response
Implement Schlick Fresnel
Implement Smith visibility
Use energy-conserving diffuse/specular balance
Validate highlight response under multiple light angles

phases.name: Normals and micro-detail
tasks: Compute SDF normals with central differences
Add procedural noise-driven surface perturbation
Modulate roughness with subtle noise
Avoid visible distortion while improving realism

phases.name: Curvature and wear
tasks: Add curvature-aware roughness variation
Darken cavities and contact areas slightly
Increase specular variation on exposed areas
Use wetness and exposure to vary surface response

phases.name: Wet surface response
tasks: Accumulate wetness on upward-facing surfaces
Reduce roughness when wet
Slightly darken wet surfaces
Increase specular intensity under rain
Keep the effect subtle and physically plausible

workstreams.name: Physical room rework
goals: Rebuild room geometry as thick architectural shells instead of thin surfaces
Support procedural openings for windows, doors, and future cutaways
Create room-local anchors and no-placement zones for future procedural interiors
Keep room structure deterministic, extensible, and performant

phases.name: Room shell data model
tasks: Define room-local thickness fields for walls, floor, and ceiling
Represent each room as an outer shell, inner shell, and structural joins
Add stable local coordinates for walls, floors, ceilings, and openings
Separate physical structure from render-only decoration

phases.name: Procedural openings
tasks: Define parametric openings with type, size, wall target, and offset metadata
Support windows as true openings with visible depth and reveal geometry
Support doors and door openings as cutaways from the shell
Keep openings deterministic and derived from the room definition

phases.name: Interior placement framework
tasks: Introduce floor, wall, and ceiling anchor regions for procedural objects
Define exclusion zones around openings, shell thickness, and trim
Expose clear room-local placement metadata for future object generation
Keep placement rules independent from mesh implementation details

phases.name: Cutaway and visibility support
tasks: Allow room cutaways to reveal the far side of the room cleanly
Keep cutaway state separate from the authoritative physical shell
Ensure interior-facing surfaces remain finished and non-destructive under section views
Prevent cutaway artifacts from affecting collision or placement data

phases.name: Legacy compatibility and rollout
tasks: Preserve existing room layouts during migration
Provide fallback behavior for rooms that do not yet define openings
Keep geometry generation event-driven rather than per-frame
Verify that new room definitions remain compatible with existing rendering and selection systems

workstreams.name: Shadow and rain refinement
goals: Improve shadow quality where it matters most
Reduce shadow cost when it is not needed
Make rain feel layered and atmospheric
Provide a path to a shader-based rain solution
Maintain temporal stability and visual consistency during motion and lighting transitions

phases.name: Shadow architecture
tasks: Use a high-quality directional light shadow map as the primary source
Tune bias and normalBias to minimize acne and peter-panning
Fit the shadow camera tightly to the playable area
Use ContactShadows for close-field grounding

phases.name: Shadow tuning workflow
tasks: Document shadow map size, camera bounds, bias, and softness settings
Create a repeatable visual QA checklist for shadow tuning
Flag shadow-casting behavior per object type where appropriate

phases.name: Adaptive shadow scaling
tasks: Reduce shadow cost when frame time rises
Scale shadow quality based on camera motion and scene complexity
Prefer graceful degradation over hard visual drops

phases.name: Rain layering
tasks: Keep lightweight volumetric precipitation
Add near-camera rain streaks with stronger parallax
Use mist near the ground and around occluders
Make surfaces respond to rain through wetness accumulation

phases.name: Screen-space rain path
tasks: Prototype a depth-aware screen-space rain shader
Compare visual quality and performance against particle rain
Retain the hybrid option if it proves best overall

strategy: Add targeted logging around shader inputs, shadow settings, weather state, and room shell generation
Validate material parameter ranges before rendering
Track frame-time impacts for shader, shadow, weather, and room geometry changes
Record before-and-after snapshots for visual regressions
Use feature flags to isolate each rendering subsystem
Instrument room opening generation with bounds, thickness, and residual geometry reporting
Expose debug overlays for shell thickness, opening volumes, and placement exclusion zones
Verify that cutaway state does not mutate the underlying physical room model

completionChecks.name: PBR plausibility
criteria: SDF highlights vary correctly with view angle and light angle
Roughness variation is visible but subtle
Wet surfaces become darker and glossier
Materials remain physically believable across presets

completionChecks.name: Shadow quality and stability
criteria: Primary shadows look stable without acne or peter-panning
Contact shadows ground objects convincingly
Shadow quality scales down gracefully under load
No major shadow flicker during camera movement
Shadow transitions remain temporally stable across camera motion and lighting changes

completionChecks.name: Rain realism and stability
criteria: Rain reads clearly in foreground, midground, and distance
Mist reinforces the rainy atmosphere without obscuring the scene
Wetness affects surfaces consistently
Rain remains performant at target frame rate
Rain motion remains stable without aliasing, popping, or distracting pattern repetition

completionChecks.name: Room physical rework validity
criteria: Walls, floor, and ceiling render with believable thickness
Windows and doors are true openings in the shell
Cutaways reveal finished interior surfaces without mutating physical structure
Room-local placement anchors and exclusion zones are available for future procedural objects
Geometry generation is deterministic and does not introduce seams, cracks, or z-fighting
Existing room layouts remain compatible or have a documented migration path

definitionOfDone: The scene uses physically plausible material behavior for key SDF objects
Lighting response is richer and more realistic
Shadow rendering is stable and performance-aware
Rain and mist are layered and atmospheric
Completion checks pass without visual regressions
Temporal stability is preserved across motion, lighting changes, and scene interaction
Rendering changes avoid unnecessary CPU-side overhead and remain GPU-friendly
Room geometry is rebuilt as a thick-shell physical system with procedural openings and future-ready placement metadata
